definition: Eccentric projection is the tendency for a sensation caused by stimulation of a nerve pathway, rather than its end organ, to be experienced as if it came from the nerve’s peripheral ending. In historical psychology, it is treated as a form of nervous projection and distinguished from using projection to mean general localization in space.
